title: Reconcile dark/high-contrast tokens, reduce focus-jank in nested tables, and assemble accessibility certification evidence
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We need to reconcile a set of legacy color tokens used by compact tables, mini charts, and button pills in dark and high-contrast modes that are causing focus outline inconsistencies (jank) and failing automated contrast checks. Additionally, we must produce a consolidated accessibility certification package (VPAT-style evidence) that demonstrates fixes and test coverage for keyboard navigation in nested table rows, chart legends, and floating action overlays.

Motivation: Several customer-reported regressions and internal accessibility audits found intermittent focus outline jumping when virtualized rows mount/unmount, inconsistent color usage across dense components, and failing WCAG contrast for a11y themes. This ticket glues design and engineering work: decide token names & ramps, implement focus-stable patterns for virtualized lists/tables, and collate evidence for an accessibility review and VPAT submission.

Scope:
- Audit and canonicalize color tokens used across compact controls (tokens: neutral-*, accent-*, focus-*, surface-*) for dark and high-contrast themes.
- Introduce a small stable focus token set for focus outlines and focus-visible behavior to reduce per-component overrides.
- Implement a focus-stable virtualization pattern for table row rehydration to eliminate tab-index/scroll-jump issues.
- Update chart legend keyboard affordances and live-region announcements for selection changes.
- Produce a VPAT-style evidence bundle (screenshots, test logs, manual checks) and link to test harness runs (NVDA/VoiceOver) for release reviewers.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- Token surface area: aim to add 4-6 new semantic tokens rather than exhaustively renaming existing legacy colors to keep migration cost low.
- Focus visuals: prefer thicker, single-color ring (semantic focus token) over multi-layer glows to keep contrast reliable across themes. This slightly changes current aesthetic but improves reliability for screen reader users and keyboard only flows.
- Virtualization approach: Implement a lightweight key-stabilization shim in the table component (ENG implementation) instead of a full rewrite of the virtualization library. Lower engineering effort and risk, may require targeted QA for edge cases.

Deliverables:
- Token spec doc in Confluence with token mappings and color ramp rationale.
- Design tokens PR with color hex values and dark/high-contrast variants.
- Component PRs: table (focus-stable virtualization), button pills, compact controls, chart legend keyboard behaviors.
- VPAT evidence bundle: test plan, screenshots, NVDA/VoiceOver logs, accessibility checklist.

Success criteria:
- All affected components pass automated contrast checks (WCAG AA) in both default dark and high-contrast themes.
- No user-reproducible focus-jump when tabbing through virtualized table rows on Chrome + VoiceOver + NVDA on supported platforms.
- VPAT evidence bundle accepted by compliance reviewer (PM sign-off) and attached to the release artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Defined semantic tokens for focus, surface, and text with dark and high-contrast variants in the token spec
Design token PR merged and gulp/build picks up new tokens without breaking other themes
Table component implements stable-key virtualization shim and disables per-row tabindex toggles during mount
Manual keyboard walkthrough (desktop and macOS) shows no focus-jump on nested rows
Chart legend supports arrow/key navigation and exposes changes to an aria-live polite region
VPAT-style evidence bundle uploaded to Confluence + linked in ticket and validated by Compliance PM
